utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. We started a bit late. To be quite honest, I do not know the reasons myself. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-03-69-T, the Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Jordash, you have finished your cross-examination, which means that now Mr. Petrovic, you're ready to start.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Milovanovic, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Petrovic. Mr. Petrovic is counsel for Mr. Simatovic. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, General.

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday in your testimony you mentioned that in October 1993 an agreement was signed between Abdic and Radovan Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have a document in front of me, but it is only in English unfortunately. It's 65 ter 2D99. It's the text of the said agreement, and since it is available only in English and the translation service was not willing to translate it since this is already in one of the official languages of the Tribunal, I would like to read out some brief passages to show whether or not this is the agreement the General spoke about yesterday. Could we please put 2D99 on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: General, I'm about to read some excerpts with the leave of the Chamber, and then please tell us whether this is what you were mentioning yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed, but this English version tells us that it is a translation of the original. So therefore I'm a bit surprised that the original would not be available. I'm even a bit surprised that you offered the document for translation, where it must be clear that there must be a B/C/S original. But apart from that, and also looking at the Prosecution whether they have any original in their possession, let me see -- I would have called extension 2456 is -- if I was seeking the original. Because it reads: "Translation from the Serbian language original by Bruno Ogorelec, Media Analysis Unit, PTO extension 2456." I would have called him to see whether there would be an original somewhere. Mr. Petrovic, this is not a level of inventivity which I thought you would not have available to yourself, isn't it? Let's proceed. And if someone calls 2456.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I can provide a very brief explanation. We offered this document to the translation service because we found it only in this English version, and we offered it to the translation service. And if I'm not mistaken their reply was that this is a document in one of the official languages of the Tribunal, that they cannot translate it. Of course this is a translation, since Abdic, Karadzic, and Milosevic struck this agreement in Serbian or Bosnia. But in order to -- not to waste time, let me try to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The issue I'm raising, why to seek a B/C/S translation if there must be an original B/C/S version; rather look for the original. That is what my message was, and let's now proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: General, the introduction of the document reads: [In English] "At the invitation of the President of the Republic of Serbia, Slobodan Milosevic, and motivated by the goal of securing a durable peace between the Serbs and Muslims in the area of the former Yugoslav Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the President of Republika Srpska, Radovan Karadzic; and the President of Autonomous Province of Western Bosnia of the Republic of Bosnia, Fikret Abdic, have met in Belgrade and decided to propose, jointly, with the involvement of the President of the Republic of Serbia, Slobodan Milosevic, the following declaration: "The Republika Srpska recognises the existence, the will of people, and the legality of the Autonomous Province of the Western Bosnia of the Republic of Bosnia, one of three constituent republics of the Union of Bosnia and Herzegovina, as defined by the Owen and Stoltenberg Peace Plan." [Interpretation] Item 3: [In English] "Presidents Radovan Karadzic and Fikret Abdic, in the name of their citizens and governments, solemnly proclaim the peace, and declare the start of the building of good neighbourly relations and universal co-operation in the fields of politics, economy, traffic, communications, culture, sports, and other fields." [Interpretation] And finally item 12. Could we please have the relevant page displayed. [Previous translation continues]... [In English] In e-court under 12: "Presidents Radovan Karadzic and Fikret Abdic expresses their gratitude to the President of the Republic of Serbia, Slobodan Milosevic, for the great contribution he has given to the arrangement of the just and durable peace between the Republic of Srpska and the Autonomous Province of Western Bosnia ... "In Belgrade, 22 October 1993." Signed by Radovan Karadzic, Fikret Abdic, and Slobodan Milosevic. [Interpretation] General, my question is: Is this the text of the agreement that you mentioned in your testimony yesterday, if I'm not mistaken, or on Friday?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never seen this text of the agreement so far. I learned from the Daily Press in the evening of the 22nd of October, I think, that this agreement was signed. My -- I wasn't -- I didn't favour that agreement at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: But, General, does what I have read out correspond to your knowledge of the contents of this agreement between the two sides that was struck in the presence of the third side?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General, do the various duties of governmental bodies of the RS, including the VRS, stem from this agreement, and I'm referring to the duties toward the autonomous province of Western Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat what he has started saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you -- one second, one second. Could you re-start your answer, because the interpreters could not hear you. Do I have to repeat the question to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then would you please re-start.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the following day, the -- a meeting of the Supreme Command of the Republika Srpska was called. Only I was invited from the Main Staff. Among the other matters that were discussed at that meeting, I put forward a question about this agreement because this agreement was called an agreement on permanent peace in the media, a peace between the Muslims and Serbs in Bosnia and Herzegovina. And I asked Karadzic, "How could you forget Alija Izetbegovic? Fikret Abdic cannot guarantee peace in all of Bosnia and Herzegovina between all Muslims and all Serbs." However, Karadzic said to me, "General, this isn't really our business, but this agreement isn't harmful to Republika Srpska, and Slobodan Milosevic likes it." So I didn't want to lose Yugoslavia as an ally or Serbia and this agreement with Abdic doesn't cost us a thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, I haven't finished. In this agreement, the VRS should have given some of its weapons to the newly established army of Fikret Abdic. That's what was put to us, and I refused that. I said that the VRS could give only those weapons that were received from the government of the RS but none of the weapons that we procured ourselves. And eventually that didn't happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I seek to tender this document as a Defence exhibit, and we will try to procure the Serbian version in the way that you suggested we should.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution would ask that it be marked for identification. Now Mr. Laugel is attempting to investigate whether there is an original and hopefully we'll have some more word in a short.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Registrar, would you assign a number to have it marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The document shall be admitted as Exhibit D00040, marked for identification. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D40 is marked for identification. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Could we please see document 65 ter 4167 on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: General, do you know this document that we can see now?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a minute. Let me see what this is. Yes, directive number 6 of the Supreme Command of the armed forces of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please display the last page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: This is a directive which was issued by the supreme commander Radovan Karadzic, and it was drafted by Colonel Radivoje Miletic; correct?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now show item 5 of this directive to the witness. In the Serbian version it's on page 4 and in the English version -- actually, it's page 4 in both linguistic versions, item 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: General, in item 5 we can read the tasks of the 2nd Krajina Corps as set out by this directive; correct?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: My question is whether this directive defines the tasks of the VRS, namely, to provide assistance to the forces of Fikret Abdic in the western part of the front, to achieve the goal of establishing autonomy, and in co-operation with the Serbian army of the Krajina?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us now look at page 5 in the Serbian, but in English we needn't turn the page. It can be seen on this page.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: The task of the 1st Krajina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could we zoom in.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the upper half of page 5 be blown up for the General, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Have you seen it, General?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that the task of the 1st Krajina Corps was to act in co-ordination with the 2nd Krajina Corps in the establishment of the autonomous province of Western Bosnia, as we see in this directive?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you please explain to us -- or I take back this one. The tasks as set out in this directive, do they mean the elimination and the destruction, by combat, of course, of the so-called 5th Corps of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which was there in that area?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since the corps were established, that has always been the goal of the VRS. Later on the Serbian army of the Krajina joined in to abet our efforts and the forces of Fikret Abdic also. It was all along the lines of that saying: The enemy of my enemy is my friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, what was the significance of the 5th Corps for the Serbian army in Krajina and the VRS?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't comment about the Serbian army of the Krajina, but the elimination of the 5th Corps of the ABiH would be -- would mean the removal of a threat to the north-west part of Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No -- no objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It's admitted as Exhibit D00041. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's admitted by our decision as D41. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Could the Court please produce P389. Could we please have page 2 in the Serbian and the last page in the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: General, is this your document, a document that you drafted?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was sent via teleprinter without a signature, but I do believe it's mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have the first page back, the first page of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: General, in the first paragraph of this document, and you see it before you, it says that the Chief of Staff and the chief of security organs of the 21st Corps of the Army of Republic of Serbian Krajina had contact with Fikret Abdic. Is this the Chief of Staff of the 21st Corps of the Army of Krajina or yourself? I'm not clear.

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Chief of Staff and the chief of security organs of the 21st Corps, of the Kordun Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please slow down and try and not to overlap.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In the second paragraph --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Milovanovic, you're invited to wait until the translation has finished and not to overlap with Mr. Petrovic and to speak relatively slowly so that we will not miss one word through the interpretation. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: General, could you please look at the second paragraph of the same report.

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which starts with the words: "At this meeting ..."?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Can I put my question to you?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just bear with me for a second, please. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: My question is this: Why was it important for Fikret Abdic to be informed about the planned offensive actions of the 2nd Krajina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose that he should have started the same time. He had his own plans to launch an offensive against the 5th Corps. That was important because of the co-ordination between the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So you're saying that the forces of Western Bosnia, as it was called, and forces of the 2nd Corps could be called co-operation with -- between the two formations?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, co-operation and not an alliance between the two militaries.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And now look at paragraph 3 of this document. My question is this: Do you know what was the nature of the relations that Fikret Abdic had with the Republic of Croatia at the time when this report was drafted?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know what his personal relations were with the Republic of Croatia. I only know what I heard and saw in the media. The day before, on the 21st of October, he signed an agreement with Mate Boban. That was also a peace agreement, but its title was a bit shorter. I don't know what the title was. I only know that Mate Boban placed the HVO forces in the Bihac region under the command of Fikret Abdic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the Court please produce 65 ter 119.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: General, could you please look at paragraph 2 in that document. This is another document which you -- or perhaps I should first show you page 3, the last page in the Serbian and in the English versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the last pages in both versions of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is this document also yours?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, it was sent in the same way but it is my document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Let's now look at page 1, paragraph 2. Could you please read paragraph 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could paragraph 2 be blown up, because I'm sure that the General is going to have problems reading it as it is. Paragraph 2. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've done it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Here a reference is made to an agreement in Vojnic between the representatives of the Army of Yugoslavia, the VRS, the Serbian Army of Krajina, and the National Defence of Western Bosnia, signed on the 24th of June, 1994. What kind of agreement was that; do you remember?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know. I was not in Vojnic. The agreement was achieved by General Mladic, who signed it with the commander of the Army of Serbian Krajina and Fikret Abdic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the contents of the agreement?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly what I've just read in paragraph 2, the gist of the agreement was for the Army of Republika Srpska or the 2nd Corps to engage the forces of the 5th Corps on the Una River, which meant that we had launch demonstrative attacks in order for the 5th Corps to engage the larger part of its troops with us and leave a smaller part of these troops to engage Fikret Abdic's forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I understand that you didn't attend the meeting, but do you know who was there on behalf of the Army of Yugoslavia when that agreement was signed?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I wasn't there. And Mladic didn't tell me who was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm just checking with Mr. Laugel, but I see that this document is marked as P381, marked for identification. I'm trying to investigate what -- who made the objection to its admission. But since it was initially tendered by the Prosecution, I certainly have no objection to its admittance now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that it was MFI'd on the 23rd of April of this year as P381.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. The objection was raised on behalf of both Defence teams. As far as we're concerned, we would like this document to be tendered and we certainly would like to hear from the other Defence team whether they agree with our proposal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We agree. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You agree. Then nothing opposes anymore the admission into evidence of P381. Therefore, P381 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Could the Court please produce 65 ter 5068. Could the General also be allowed to see page 2 in the B/C/S version, and for the others in the courtroom could the last page in the English version be displayed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: General, this document was signed by Major-General Borislav Djukic. Do you know this gentleman? Do you know who General Djukic was?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was an officer, or rather, a general of the Serbian army of Krajina. The assistant of General Novakovic, I knew him as a logistics man, but I heard that he was also the Chief of Staff and I suppose that he signed this document in his capacity as the Chief of Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at paragraph 3 of the document. In the Serbian language it is towards the top of page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, could the paragraph please be blown up for the benefit of the General, who might have a problem reading this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you please read paragraph 3, General.

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you want me to do it aloud or just for myself?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Just for yourself because we can all see. We can all read the document at the same time you do.

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. My question to you is this: This operation that was described here, do you know who drafted the plan for this operation here? Could we ascribe it to the author of the document, or was it somebody else who did it.

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I please be shown the heading of this letter or report? I would like to see the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: The date is the 9th of July, 1995 [as interpreted]. We can show you the heading as well, but in order to save some time --

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by the style and by the ignorance - if I may say so - this document was certainly not drafted in the General Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska. And if you are asking for my opinion, I believe that it was drafted by this same General Djukic, as the assistant for logistics in the command of the Army of Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender this document into evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Admitted as Exhibit D00042. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D42 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I need to make a correction. This is what I owe to the Trial Chamber and to the General. On page 15 and line 4 it says that the document was drafted on the 9th of July, 1995, whereas the document is actually drafted on the 9th of July, 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the copy that I'm looking at says "1993," the translation that I'm looking at.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the original reads 1994, and the events described happened in 1994. Can we please have the first page of the document displayed both in English and in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There seems to be a translation error in the translation because the original clearly refers to 1994, whereas the translation refers to 1993. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore your correction was accurate. Although it's not dramatic, I'd rather have the translation replaced by one without errors.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. We shall do that, Your Honours. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the Court please produce 65 ter 5070.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: This is another document drafted by General Borislav Djukic. General, could you please look at paragraph 2. The document is dated the 12th of July, 1994. In the heading it says the Republic of Serbian Krajina, the Main Staff of the Army of Serbian Krajina. This is to avoid any dilemmas as to where the document originates from. Could you please look at paragraph 2, and I'll have some questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. What I would like to know is this: Based on this operative report, can we conclude that on the previous day or during a previous period, the forces of the 2nd Krajina Corps of the Army of Republika Srpska carried out defence operations and whether they co-operated with the forces of the Serbian Army of Krajina and the forces of the Western Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. President, I need your assistance, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm analysing documents which I did not draft myself, which do not originate from the Army of Republika Srpska. I don't know whether I'm a witness or an analyst here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are here as a witness, and you are asked now whether we can conclude based on this report that something had happened on the previous day. Now, if you have any knowledge what happened on the previous day, please tell us; if you just draw your conclusions on the basis of the report, perhaps a witness of fact is not the most appropriate person to do so -- unless you would have any special understanding of these kind of documents which would make it possible for you to draw conclusions which another -- someone analysing the document would not be able to make. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I ask that we go into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has it to do with what the witness just --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Perhaps, Your Honour, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- asked --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: -- maybe I can say -- but -- I'll say something in public session, maybe it will indicate what I'm thinking to the Chamber. The last two exhibits are the subject of a pending 54 bis application with respect to RFA 1333, and perhaps it would be more prudent that they be introduced -- placed under seal until that application is decided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that seems to be ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it the Defence teams do not oppose that. The last two exhibits are -- that were shown to the witness are under seal. So the admission of the previous one and the one shown at this moment to the witness should not be shown to the public. Mr. Petrovic, there are two options: Either you rephrase your question, or we hear from the witness, who would then keep in mind what I just said about his position. What would you prefer?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will rephrase my question and ask about a unit belonging to the army in which the General was the deputy commander --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: General, do you know that the 2nd Krajina Corps in July 1994 acted in co-ordination with the Serbian Army of the Krajina and the forces of people's defence from the Western Bosnia autonomous province in Cazinska Krajina and along the axes that are mentioned here?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I seek to tender this document into evidence as well, but I don't know if what Mr. Groome said applies to this one as well. If it does, then this one should also be admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I understood his reference to the last two documents as the last one which was admitted and the present one who was discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. I have no objection to admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Registrar, the number for this exhibit would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D00043. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D00043 is admitted into evidence under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Could we now please see 65 ter 2D00087.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. 2D00087, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: This is also a document of the Republic of Serbian Krajina, namely, the Main Staff of the Army of Serbian Krajina, and it was signed by one Borislav Djukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's turn to page 2 on the Serbian version. It's on page 2, suggested measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: General, please look at these measures, and then I will put my question to you.

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just find it. Oh, yes, I've found it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Have you read it, General?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not yet, not all of it. The first line of item 4 is totally illegible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I'll read it out to you. "To prevent Velika Kladusa from falling on the 9th of March, it is necessary to strengthen the defence with at least an armoured battalion." Some parts of it are illegible, I will admit.

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The illegible part means "or an infantry company."

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, we have interpreted it together. Can I put my question now?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is General Djukic suggesting measures here and activities that make it necessary for both the VRS and the forces of the Autonomous Province of Western Bosnia and the Serbian Army of the Krajina to act?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his answer. The speakers are kindly reminded not to overlap, and make a pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Milovanovic, could I again ask you not to start answering the question when the interpreters are still interpreting the words spoken by Mr. Petrovic, so to make a brief pause. And could I also invite you to repeat your last answer. Should I repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That isn't necessary. The signatory of the document, General Djukic, under item 5 of the suggested measures, only informs his units that the 2nd Krajina Corps of the VRS continues the attack it started yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It will be admitted as Exhibit D00044. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D44 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Let us look at 65 ter 2D119.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: General, please tell us whether this is one of your documents.

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, is this document in essence about singling out the 3rd Battalion of the 11th lpbr and sending it, as we see under item 3, the battalion will be used in accordance with the decisions of the Pauk command; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The number would be, Mr. Registrar ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D00045. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D45 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Could we please show the General 65 ter 2D71.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: General, please take a look at this document and tell us if this is a document of the commander Colonel-General Ratko Mladic. But if I can tell, the assistant commander for legal affairs has signed.

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot see the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please scroll down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The signature of General Mladic isn't there. The document wasn't sent by teleprinter; it was typed. And it says: The copy of the order is being certified by assistant commander for morale and legal affairs, General Simic. But I don't know the man.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at the introduction.

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: The command of the 1st Zvornik Brigade. So let us simplify. My question is: Do you know that Colonel-General Ratko Mladic, upon the proposal of the commander of the Serbian Army of the Krajina Lieutenant-General Mile Novakovic, commanded the combat group Mauzer belonging to the Serbian army of the Krajina and another unit?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: General, if you look at the stamp on this document - can we please see it - does that stamp look like that of a unit of the VRS, in particular here the 1st Zvornik Brigade? Was this a stamp as was used by brigade-level units of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the stamp used by the units of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, the number would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit Number D00046.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D46 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we please see 65 ter 4216, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: This is a document of the people's defence of Western Bosnia, their Supreme Command. I'll ask you to take a look at items 7 and 8, where we see the names Mile Novakovic, commander of Pauk; and Cedo Bulat, chief of the command of Pauk. My question is: Does this correspond to your knowledge of who the commander and the chief in the command of Pauk was?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Groome, is there any dispute about who the commander of Pauk and the -- who the chief of the command of Pauk was?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I don't believe so, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Why are we hearing evidence where there seems to be no dispute about these kind of matters, Mr. Petrovic? Why not agree with Mr. Groome on these matters, and then if you want, if need be, the document -- we are here to focus on matters which are in dispute and not on matters which are not in dispute.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. We will certainly bear in mind what you said, and we have already started drafting a list of facts that we want to offer our learned friends for their acceptance. Due to the well-known circumstances, the job isn't finished yet, but we are working on it and we will send it to the -- to our colleagues. If I may, I would like to proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but, meanwhile, whatever you want to establish, please ask yourself at this moment, even if the list is not ready - and not blaming you for it, the circumstances explained, it should have been done already before these circumstances arose - but ask yourself -- I mean, if I can imagine that this might not be a highly disputed issue, you would be able to consider that as well I would say. For any of your next questions, please ask yourself whether that's anything you would expect Mr. Groome to disagree with.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: May I just -- hopefully assisting the Court, it is, I understand, from reading the Prosecution's evidence to be called, their case that certain members, including number 12 on this list, would only take orders from the accused. And so to that extent, in our submission, these are extremely relevant. The commander isn't disputed, but how the operation worked is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But what we are doing here is asking was Mr. X or was Mr. Y -- so whether they were effective in their command and who would listen to them, that may be disputed matters, but apparently not this, what is -- he is called here "commander." And we are talking about -- not about Mr. 12, is it, we are talking about, I think, 7 and 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, I suppose -- it's just that these exhibits, in our submission, are relevant insofar as they go to prove other aspects of the Prosecution case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but the question -- the one and only question put to this witness is: Is it in accordance with your recollection that he was this and he was that, which is -- apparently is a matter which is not in dispute.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'll sit down, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I addressed Mr. Groome when he had said that he had no objections to admission. Mr. Registrar, the number under which it would be admitted would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D00047, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D47 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: General, according to what you know, was General Novakovic in command of the units that were resubordinated to the Pauk command?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And now I would like to ask you just a few more questions about Pauk, but I would kindly ask you to answer either yes or no, so we may bring this topic to an end, if you agree to do so and if you can, of course. First question, therefore: Is it true that the strategic interests of the Army of Republika Srpska was to weaken and eliminate the 5th Corps from the very beginning of the war to the end of 1995?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that from 1993 the command was carried out based on the co-operation and co-ordination of all units involved in this activity?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that the Pauk command is only a different organisational form of co-operation and co-ordination of the kind that existed even before the end of 1994?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I did not understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that the Pauk command is an organisational form of co-operation and co-ordination which in its essence was identical to the co-operation and co-ordination which existed even before the Pauk command was set up?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was a temporary force to carry out a certain task.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that even after the establishment of the Pauk command, the strategic goals of all involved parties remained the same in everything, and that concerns the Army of Republika Srpska, the Army of Serbian Krajina, and the National Defence of Western Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the main task was to break up the 5th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that we have reached the time for our first break, if you're agreeable; and after that, I will be moving on to a different topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and could you inform us also whether you are on schedule?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe so. For the time being I would say so, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll have a break, and we resume at 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: General, now I would like to move on to a different topic. Could we now please look at a document first, and then I will ask you for your comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is 65 ter 4653. Could the Court please produce the document. Can we first see page 2 in the Serbian language and page 2 in the English language.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: General, this is a directive on the use of armed forces in the upcoming period dated 10th of December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please look at the last pages, both in the Serbian and the English versions of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: The directive was signed by the federal secretary for National Defence, army general Veljko Kadijevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see the third page, both in the Serbian original and the English translation. Can we see the top of those two pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: General, could you please read the first paragraph on the page currently displayed on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Starting with the word "our"?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. My question is this: The federal secretary Kadijevic, do you understand him and the way he drafted his directive? Did he define the protection of the Serbian population as the ultimate aim of the war? Is that the way you understood the secretary -- federal secretary's directive?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To me personally there is something contradictory here, something controversial. "Our armed forces are entering a new period of exceptional significance for accomplishing the ultimate aims of the war ..." and we're talking about December 1991. I suppose that he means the war between Croatia and the then-Republic of Serbian Krajina, i.e., the activities of the JNA. I don't have any particular opinion about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: But do you then accept that the federal secretary defines the ultimate goal as protection of the Serbian population in the territory where the -- that population resides outside of Serbia, implying Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina? Is that the way you would understand the ultimate goal of the war as defined by Kadijevic?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please slow down when putting his questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, I don't understand your question, despite my best wishes to understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, let's take the opportunity and if you agree so admit this document into evidence if the witness can confirm that the document was drafted by the federal secretary. If you think that that might be useful, then I would like to tender this document into evidence; if not, I will move on. It is the Prosecutor's 65 ter document, so I suppose that the Prosecutor also intended at one point to use this document or even tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no objection to the admittance of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's rather unclear what it serves. Is there any dispute about this document coming from Mr. Kadijevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Not from the Prosecution, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. So therefore we don't need it. What you asked the witness -- well, he said: I can't comment on it. And if you intended to -- to establish that what the document says is that the ultimate aims of the war, whatever war that may have been, was the protection of the Serbian population, that's what the document says. So therefore I still do not see the relevance, but perhaps it takes more time to discuss it than -- Mr. Registrar, the number would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D00048.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D48 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Could the Court please produce 65 ter 94, another Prosecutor's 65 ter document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: General, I believe that the Prosecutor has already showed you this document, that it was shown to you during your proofing session. This document bears the title: "Conclusions from the appraisal of the situation in Bosnia-Herzegovina," and the document was drafted by General Milutin Kukanjac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at paragraph 3(c) on page 2 in the Serbian language. I will have one question for the General.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: It's at the very bottom of the page, General.

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under (c)?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The situation in the JNA territory under (c). Just the first sentence. Let's not waste much time.

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Generally speaking" --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but read it to yourself. No need to read it aloud. Just the first sentence, please, and then I'll have a question to you. Here the General is of the opinion that the SDS and the Serbian people at the time when the document was drafted, which was in March 1992, accepted the army, co-operated with the commands, and the Serbs responded eagerly and joined voluntary and war units. My question to you is this: Did you have the same opinion as General Kukanjac? Did you share General Kukanjac's opinion with regard to the initial period and the relationship between the SDS, the Serbian population, and the JNA?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any information about any of that, because at the time I was in Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If that is indeed the case, let's move on and look at paragraph 5 in the same document which is on page 3 in B/C/S. Could you please look at paragraph 5.

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Voluntary units"?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And it says here that the strength of voluntary units amounts to 69.198 men, that's under (b), and then under (f) -- I'm going to read to speed up --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, speeding up for the interpreters is not something they are wishing you to do, but could we move to the next page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Actually, it's one page before in the English version, if I could have that displayed, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you referred to under (b) and under (f), the strength of voluntary units, so that was on --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it is my impression that you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I read from the transcript. It says here that the strength of voluntary units amounts to 69.198. That is on the page which we see now on our screen, and that's what you referred to. So that's the reason why I asked for the next page to be shown, because the previous page in English showed only paragraph (a). But if there's anything you would like to read from (a), please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I actually did not see what was displayed. I wanted to look at Article 5(b), and now I would like to read from Article 5(f). I wanted to read in order to speed things along.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What it says under (f) is that: "The JNA has distributed" --

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "51.900 pieces of weaponry" --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so. "The JNA has distributed 51.900 weapons and the SDS 17.298 pieces of weaponry ..." My question to you, General, is this: Do you have any information that would confirm what General Kukanjac wrote about the number of pieces of weaponry that the JNA had distributed to the population during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, is that in dispute about these numbers distributed by the JNA for 75 per cent and the SDS for the remaining 25 per cent?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, and the Prosecution would not object if this document were tendered. So perhaps -- it doesn't seem that General Milovanovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any dispute about it?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Why are we asking all kind of things where they seem not to be in dispute, Mr. Petrovic? I mean, I think these numbers have come up in other cases several times, even from what I remember, presented by the Prosecution. So it's not clear to me -- you're asking whether this is correct, and the Prosecution already agrees to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your leave, I would like to say that one part of the Prosecutor's case against the accused is that they contributed significantly to the armament of the population in the territories that we are referring to here. What we would like to show in this case are the facts about who, how, and to what extent armed the population. This is what we wanted to do. If the Prosecution wants to withdraw their -- that part of the case, then confirm that the accused did not have anything whatsoever to do in all that, that's all good and fine, and we will move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, what Mr. Petrovic says is that you're undermining your own case by admitting to these numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, arms were provided to the territories by a number of sources. I'm not willing to agree that the two accused had no part to play, but I don't see that they exclude each -- one excludes the other. I'm willing to agree that the JNA provided arms, as described by General Kukanjac, but whether I'm willing to go so far as to immunise the two accused from having engaged in activities related to arming civilians, I'm not willing to go so far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, Mr. Petrovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. What I see is that apparently this is about zones, et cetera, so therefore it might be -- to say, Is this number correct or is it not correct, rather than look at where they were distributed, when they were distributed, in order -- I mean, that perhaps makes sense, but the numbers in itself -- okay. Let's move on and -- but I want to stress that for the Chamber to be assisted by the evidence you're eliciting, it should be clear where exactly the dispute is and for us not to guess. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if my learned friend accepts the figures that appear in this document, this will save us a significant amount of time; namely, that the JNA distributed 51.900 weapons before the war. And we don't have to proceed with this document at all if the Prosecutor does not insist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So what apparently you're seeking to say, we can save time if the Prosecution agrees with the numbers, that's 51.000 being distributed by the JNA and 17.298 distributed by the SDS. Do we need periods? Do we need --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it's more accurate to say I don't dispute these figures. I have no personal knowledge about the exact amount of weapons, but certainly the Prosecution does not dispute the fact that large amounts of weapons were distributed. And perhaps outside of court time if Mr. Petrovic wants to draft that into a written agreement I'd be happy to discuss that with him and I'm sure we can come to some agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, what these numbers mean, you would say, in relation to this case, that's another matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I will no longer ask questions about this document, but since this is a document that the OTP wanted to rely upon in its case, I seek to tender it into evidence. And certainly we will be only too glad to discuss it on the basis that has just been put forward.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I take it that you want to rely upon it as well because tendering into evidence is not a service to the other party. Mr. Registrar, the number would be ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D49 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed. I'm not specifically asking the Stanisic Defence at any time, but I take it that you'll jump up if there's any objection against the document which is tendered by the other Defence team. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: General, let us look at 65 ter 4685. Tell us, please, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see the last page for the witness to be able to see the signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, do you recognise the document on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's the first directive issued by the commander, General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you take part in drafting this directive?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I probably did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know which other officers, apart from General Mladic, officers from the Main Staff, took part in the drafting of this directive, if you know?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see or look at item 4 of this directive which is on page 2 in the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please read the centre paragraphs that appear on the screen, and then I will ask you about it.

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean paragraph (C)?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: "(C) Open for traffic," et cetera, and the following. Up until the "tasks of the units." We'll look at that later.

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Here in item 4, as the second stage, what is mentioned is creating a corridor between Semberija and Krajina, push back the enemy from the road, et cetera. My question is: What was the significance of the corridor between Semberija and the Krajina? Could you provide a brief explanation.

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the early days of the war, the Banja Luka region, that is, the Bosnian Krajina and the Knin Krajina, were cut off from Serbia, that is, they were cut off from the entire world. We were unable to supply basic foodstuffs to the population, and 12 babies died in Banja Luka hospitals because there was no -- not enough oxygen. One died ten years later, died of the consequences. There was a decision of the Presidency, the Supreme Command wasn't yet in existence, that decision being that the forces of the 1st Eastern Bosnia Corps should be used to cut through the corridor to establish a link between Bosnian Krajina with Semberija and Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you please explain. When you say "Presidency," you mean the Presidency of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please tell us -- tell us about the command of the operation of the cutting through of the corridor. Who were the members of the commanding staff for that operation?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Operation corridor 92 was commanded by the command of the 1st Corps, and it was the 1st Krajina Corps that acted in co-ordination with the Eastern Bosnia Corps, and they carried out the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now take a look at item 5, tasks of the units. Look at that section, and I'll ask you some questions about it.

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It says that the: "Tasks of the 1st Krajina Corps from OG Doboj were to continue along the directions Derventa-Modrica and Doboj-Podnovlje;" correct?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know which units were -- belonged to the OG Doboj and who commanded them?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: OG Doboj was initially commanded by the then-colonel and present-day general, Slavko Lisica. OG Doboj comprised mostly units from the surroundings of Doboj and units from Mount Ozren.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's turn the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I'll read it, if you agree, so we can speed it up. It says: "The East Bosnian Corps defends the current lines with one part of its forces."

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: The first paragraph up there.

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it. I read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: This says that: "The East Bosnian Corps, in co-ordinated action with the 1st Krajina Corps, will liberate Modrica, take the bridges over the Sava River, and provide secure traffic from Modrica to Bosanski Samac." What I'm interested to know is what the significance of this line of communication between Modrica and Samac is.

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The significance was establishing a link between Doboj and Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now please look at the section that refers to the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it. I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Would the successful accomplishment of this task mean establishing control of all territories around the city of Sarajevo? Because I don't really understand this well enough.

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wouldn't mean establishing control of the city of Sarajevo, only the taking of those parts of Sarajevo with a majority Serb population.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please take a look at the following paragraph, the last one in this document.

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the Herzegovina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: It's also -- it also refers to Sarajevo-Romanija Corps when you have read it. It said: "Unblock the road Sarajevo-Trnovo."

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Why is the unblocking of that road important?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To establish a link between Sarajevo and Kalinovik, that is, Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell us when the town of Trnovo was liberated, if you know.

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know when it was occupied and also when it was liberated. It was occupied on the 2nd of August, 1992. It was liberated on the 11th of July, 1993, as part of the -- an operation of the VRS called Lukavac 93.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that keeping Trnovo was crucial important to preserve that vital communication in the eastern part of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, if you know -- so if you know, in the summer of 1992 did the actions of the opposing side threaten that communication line you have just mentioned, that road?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. At that time I was in Drvar, and I organised defence against the Croatian Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So if I understood you correctly, you have no knowledge about that?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no knowledge about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D00050.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D50 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please show directive number 7, which is 65 ter 1178. Can we please see page 2. Number 3 in the Serbian, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: General, is this directive number 7 of the Supreme Command of the armed forces of Republika Srpska dated the 8th of March, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: The directive was issued by the supreme commander, Radovan Karadzic; right?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown paragraph 5 on page 7 in B/C/S. Page 7 according to the markings that are on the document. However, in e-court the document has some blank pages. If you could look at the bottom of the pages, you will see the numbering. What we see on the screen now is number 3, and we're looking for number 5, page number 5. The last three ERN digits are 171. I apologise, I need page 7 and not page 5. I said 7 in the Serbian. I'm sure that's it. There must be something with the interpretation. Now we have it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you please read the tasks of the 2nd Krajina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: My question to you is this: The contents of directive number 7 with regard to the part of the front line in the area of responsibility of the 2nd Krajina Corps, does it -- do they represent the continuity with regard to the previous directives that concern that part of the front line?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender this document into evidence if there are no objections from the Prosecution bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's already MFI'd by the Prosecution as P388, and therefore I suggest that we admit it as P388. P388 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could the witness please be shown 2D114, 65 ter 2D114. This is the first page. And can now the last page be displayed for the signature that's on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: General, are you the author of the document?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In addition to the request that we see before us, during the war were there some other requests sent to the General Staff of the army requesting assistance with armaments and military equipment?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: According to what you know and according to how you see this, were such requests customary between countries or entities which fostered friendly relations and of which one was a party involved in a war conflict?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know if this request of yours was approved and how much of what was requested was eventually placed at the disposal of the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This request was never approved.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know of any other similar or identical requests which fared differently?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not send any other requests. If there were any sent, they were sent by the logistics sector, and I don't know whether they were approved or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender this document into evidence as Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is admitted as D00051. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D51 is admitted into evidence. Mr. Petrovic, have you dealt with this document, because the Chamber's wondering what you are establishing at this moment and where it fits into either undermining the Prosecution case or supporting your own case. Now, I'm not -- I do not want to trigger any conversation about these matters which might influence the witness, but it's not entirely clear to us. If you'd move to an unrelated subject, the Chamber would like very much to hear in three or four lines from you where it should put this information it has just received in its thoughts. So I leave it to you whether you do that at this moment or whether you do it when you move to another subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this brings one topic to an end. There are very few things that remain. I can tell you just briefly that we're coming back to the topic of logistics, a subject that we already broached. The issue is whether the accused in this case had anything to do with the logistics support provided to the forces indicated in the indictment. This is the topic, and I will not have any more questions about that topic. However, by your leave I would like to move on to something entirely different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so we have to understand that this one request which was denied and where the witness could not inform us about other requests, not knowing anything about how it was denied, who dealt with the matter, whether this was -- whether there are several logistic avenues or not, you would say this establishes that since this request was denied -- by whom exactly? That therefore --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, of course I did not know nor could I assume what the witness's answers were going to be. We have discovered the document. I thought that I should put questions to the witness, the witness answered, and that's the situation as it is at the moment. And we will continue dealing with the subject in the future as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that you're handicapped by not having a written statement of the witness available which could serve as guidance for your questioning. It's good that you emphasize this again, that you're in a similar position as, to some extent, as the Prosecution was when calling this witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: General, sir, I would like to try and deal with a few things, or rather, clarify a few things from your testimony provided yesterday. You spoke about Arkan and about his arrival in Bijeljina. My question to you is this: Do you know who had invited Arkan to come to Bijeljina? And would you accept my suggestion that he had arrived at the invitation of Biljana Plavsic, at Biljana Plavsic's invitation?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What period are you referring to? 1992 or 1995?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: My mistake. I should have been more precise. The year is 1992. Would you agree that he had been invited by Biljana Plavsic and the local leaders of the Territorial Defence? And I'm talking about the year 1992.

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know at whose invitation he arrived. I believe that he came of his own will, that he was not even invited.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could the witness please be shown a short video-clip from the Prosecutor's 65 ter 596. The whole clip last --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the times slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are transcripts available. They're in e-court. I've been asked to repeat the times. One hour, 48 minutes, 30 seconds, to one hour, 52 minutes, 40 seconds. I don't know whether that has been recorded. The transcript is on file, and it has been distributed to the booths. Can the clip please be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Reporter Vukasinovic: You are a member of a mixed delegation that arrived in Bijeljina to witness the alleged destruction that the media in Sarajevo talk about. Is that your impression? "Biljana Plavsic: What I have seen in town as I was driving by car, not just me but my escorts, we paid a lot of attention to all that to see whether we would come across shattered glass or broken shop windows as had been portrayed by the media in Sarajevo. We did not see any of that. There was a remark uttered that the first shop that would have been broken into would be the one with shoes, but nothing of the kind could be as I saw. Entering in town my impression -- it was not an impression of entering a robbed town. The people were very happy when we arrived. They were -- welcomed us cordially, and it was my impression that the people had the feeling that they were saved from a great evil. "Reporter Vukasinovic: I have another question. You are a member of the mixed delegation; however, the second part of the delegation with Fikret Abdic and representatives of the army are not with you. It is strange that they didn't go to -- that they went to the barracks first. "Biljana Plavsic: First of all, let me tell you that I directed the entire thing. The first barricades that I came across was our -- there was a Serbian MP at the barricade who said that I should be the one to determine where to go. The column was much longer because there were representatives of the European Community as well. I told them that they didn't have to go with us; however, they met us in Tuzla and I warned them yesterday that I did not want them to go with us.
